tier_reason: Independent third-party CI suite (ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark, v8-v7 code forked from mozilla/arewefastyet, results dated 10/5/2026) lists ladybird Score 691 vs duktape 489 vs quickjs 1217 on ubuntu and 1169 vs 905 vs 1761 on macos-arm64, with per-test rows matching the record. The LibJS binary comes from Ladybird's public js-and-wasm-artifacts.yml (cmake --preset Distribution, clang), but the runners' CPU models are not stated, so not A; B matches the ChakraCore, v8, njs and quanta precedents on this suite.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: LibJS: Ladybird's own CI artifact from .github/workflows/js-and-wasm-artifacts.yml ('Package the js repl as a binary artifact'), built with cmake --preset Distribution and clang/clang++ (-DENABLE_CI_BASELINE_CPU=ON, ladybird-ci:2026.08.28 container) on Linux and the Distribution preset on macOS, fetched by ahaoboy/ladybird-js-build build.sh. Duktape: unreleased master (version string 2.99.99) cloned and built by ahaoboy/duktape-build with Duktape's default Makefile target, whose CCOPTS_NONDEBUG is -Os -fomit-frame-pointer -fno-stack-protector.
corrections.caveats: Third-party CI suite with one run per daily snapshot and no runner CPU model. The Duktape baseline is a size-optimized (-Os) build of unreleased master, which handicaps it; LibJS uses Ladybird's Distribution preset. LibJS is slower than Duktape on RegExp (66 vs 129 on Ubuntu, 114 vs 244 on macOS) and faster on the other seven tests (Crypto 1025 vs 783). It beats only Duktape, not QuickJS (1217 Ubuntu, 1761 macOS), among the listed baselines, and the suite's Time(s) row shows LibJS taking longer overall (79 s vs 70 s Ubuntu, 53 s vs 46 s macOS). The suite page leaves LibJS's version cell blank. LibJS ships only inside the Ladybird browser monorepo (no separate release found), so embedding it means pulling in Ladybird's own libraries; no Windows build is benchmarked. Per a search snippet (Ladybird newsletter, page not opened), LibJS runs an assembly bytecode interpreter; the Cranelift JIT in recent builds is for LibWasm.

notes: All numbers check against the README tables (ubuntu and macos-arm64, 10/5/2026). Main shortcomings: wins only over a -Os Duktape master build, loses to QuickJS by 1.5-1.8x and to Duktape on RegExp, and LibJS is not a standalone embeddable library. Metadata (BSD-2-Clause, 66.4k stars, last commit 2026-10-06, not a fork) confirmed on github.com.

tier_reason: Independent third-party shootout (r-lyeh-archived/scriptorium, 525 stars, Unlicense) with public harness (bench.cc, run.bat, tests/fib.lly, tests/fib.js, lily/make.bat and javascript/duktape/make.bat, both cl /Ox /Oy /MT /DNDEBUG) lists lily 2.005 s (row 17) vs duktape 9.544 s (row 32) and Lua 1.341 s. Not A because the CPU is given only as 'AMD A10 3.8 GHz' without a model number; B matches the chibi-scheme, Pawn, Neko and TinyVM precedents.

corrections.baseline: Duktape 1.2.2 (per javascript/duktape/duktape.h in the scriptorium repo), built with cl /Ox /Oy /MT /DNDEBUG; the same table lists PUC Lua at 1.341 s, where this engine is slower
corrections.compiler_and_flags: VS2015 RC (lily/make.bat: cl /Ox /Oy /MT /DNDEBUG /Dinline= /Dstrerror_r= psapi.lib); Duktape 1.2.2 built with cl /Ox /Oy /MT /DNDEBUG (javascript/duktape/make.bat); Lua's flags not stated
corrections.workload: Recursive fib(34) (tests/fib.lly vs tests/fib.js) run as a separate process through bench.exe: each session averages 5 launches (run.bat '@bench 5') of whole-process wall time including start-up, and the README table keeps the minimum session average per engine; July 2015 snapshot.
corrections.caveats: Eleven-year-old snapshot (July 2015) on one recursive-fib test; the author says 'Take it with a grain of salt'. Timings include process start-up and the table keeps each engine's best session (bench.csv shows Duktape from 9.54 s to 14.30 s across sessions, and Lily 2.31 s in the first session). The baseline is Duktape 1.2.2, far older than current releases, and fib.js calls a global fibR (a property lookup per call in Duktape) while fib.lly calls a statically bound define. PUC Lua is 1.341 s in the table, so Lily is about 1.5x slower than Lua there, although in the first logged session Lily (2.31 s) edged Lua (2.36 s), so the Lua ordering is within run-to-run noise. Scriptorium is archived and links the project under its old owner (jesserayadkins/lily); the 2015 Lily tested uses old syntax and is far older than the current code.

notes: Numbers match the scriptorium README and bench.csv. The record's claim that per-engine flags and the Duktape version are not stated was wrong: make.bat files give /Ox /Oy /MT /DNDEBUG and duktape.h says 1.2.2. Main shortcomings: one 2015 fib(34) micro-benchmark with start-up in the timing, an old Duktape 1.2.2 baseline, slower than PUC Lua; metadata (MIT, 1.1k stars, last commit 2026-09-22) confirmed.
